linguistic_propositions.proposition: The Form I agent participle is built by lengthening the vowel after the first radical and assigning kasra to the second radical, with the three radicals kept in order.
The kasra on the second radical is the exponent that separates this template from other nominal templates built on the same skeleton.
Any triliteral root yields an agent participle on this template.
A weak second radical is realised as a hamza in the participle rather than as the underlying weak letter.
A weak final radical yields a shortened indefinite form whose ending reduces to a tanwin kasra.
Roots whose final radical is hamza belong to the same deformation class as final-weak roots.
An agent participle can govern a following noun in the accusative exactly as its verb would.
The feminine of an agent participle is formed by suffixing the feminine marker.
The intensive broken-plural template is the normal plural for agent participles used as occupational nouns.
The participle expresses a standing quality or professional identity while the imperfect verb expresses a particular event in progress.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The Form I patient participle is built by prefixing م with fatha and inserting a long u between the second and third radicals.
Agent and patient participles form systematic pairs from a single root, separated by the presence of the prefix and by the vowel skeleton.
The resulting template consists of four syllables.
A weak second radical prevents the full long-u realisation, so the template shortens and takes the vowel corresponding to the weak radical.
An initial hamza is preserved on its seat and does not block the template.
Doubled roots retain both identical radicals rather than collapsing them under this template.
The patient participle expresses the result of an action already completed.
Patient participles take sound plurals by default.
One entry in the everyday-vocabulary table assigns a fourth-form base a participle carrying the Form I prefix vowel rather than the derived-form prefix.
The second-form patient participle uses a م prefix with damma and a geminated second radical carrying fatha.
Several members have lexicalised into ordinary nouns whose participial value is no longer synchronically active.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The elative is built by prefixing a hamza with fatha to the triliteral base and assigning fatha to the second radical.
One and the same shape serves for both degrees, and the degree is fixed by construction, not by form.
The elative is derived from adjectives rather than from verbs.
Most triliteral adjectives yield an elative on this template.
In the comparative construction with a مِن complement the elative is invariable and does not agree.
The definite-article construction and the annexation construction exclude the مِن complement.
The feminine counterpart is required when the elative modifies a definite feminine noun attributively.
Doubled bases merge the final two radicals under a shadda instead of showing them separately.
The lesson labels the doubled-base group with the term that conventionally names hollow bases.
Items denoting sequence and otherness belong to the elative inventory alongside the gradable items.
The elative shape is unambiguous once formed, so it can be recognised by shape alone.

The relational adjective expresses a permanent attribute while a prepositional phrase expresses a current location.

proposed_new_units.summary: Ownership and derivation rules for the relational suffix: the final geminated yaa together with its preceding kasra belongs to the affix layer and never to the root; the base's final feminine marker is deleted and certain final long vowels are dropped or converted before suffixation; agreement tails stack outside the suffix; and tokens whose base is unrecoverable abstain rather than receiving a root reading.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-s01 lists yaa in its augment inventory but treats affix ownership generically. It has no rule deleting the base's final feminine marker, no account of the base-alteration cases, and no procedure for stacking agreement tails on top of a derivational suffix, so a relational token can pass its checks while still receiving a root that swallows the suffix.

instructional_purpose: Introduces annexation as the language's principal way of relating two nouns directly, with no linking particle. It fixes the two roles, the morphological suppressions on the head, the invariant genitive on the dependent, the inheritance of definiteness, and the extension of the construction into chains.
concepts_taught: annexation as a direct two-noun relation replacing a possessive verb
the head and dependent roles and their names
suppression of tanwin on the head
prohibition of the definite article on the head

definiteness of the whole phrase inherited from the dependent

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Two nouns placed in the annexation relation express possession or association without any intervening particle.
The head loses its tanwin when it enters the construction.
The head can never carry the definite article.
The dependent is always in the genitive.
The head's case is assigned by its own function in the sentence and is independent of the construction.
The definiteness of the whole phrase is inherited from the dependent.
The construction divides into exactly three semantic types: possessive, descriptive and material.
The label used for the descriptive type is the same term the tradition uses for a structurally different subtype of annexation.
In a chain only the final member may carry the definite article or tanwin, and every non-initial member is genitive.
The absence of a possessive verb in the language is what motivates the construction.
A part-whole relation is analysed in the worked examples although it is not among the three types the lesson enumerates.

proposed_new_units.summary: Licensing table for annexation: which exponents the head may not carry (tanwin, the definite article, and the dual and sound-plural final consonant), the invariant genitive on the dependent, definiteness inheritance from the final member, the chain rule that only the last member may carry a definiteness exponent, and the participial subtype recorded as the licensed exception that both admits the article on the head and blocks definiteness inheritance.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: The committed capability matrix files annexation as a family with no instructional support and no fixtures, and names an annexation unit as remaining work. u-n03 lists the construct head as one governor type but carries no construction-internal rules; u-n01 marks case without the definiteness and exponent-suppression facts. Neither can decide whether an adjacent noun pair is an annexation at all.

instructional_purpose: Introduces the adverbial of time and place as an accusative complement, explaining the containment metaphor behind its classical name and grounding its case in an implicit locative preposition. It supplies a working inventory of items in both classes and connects the ones that require a dependent to the annexation construction taught immediately before.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The adverbial is a noun that specifies the time or place in which the action occurs, and the classical term encodes that containment.
All adverbials of time and place take the accusative.
The accusative on the adverbial does the work of the locative preposition, so a bare accusative and a prepositional phrase are equivalent.
The adverbial is an object of the verb in the same sense that a direct object is, differing only in the relation it expresses.
The two adverbials expressing sequence in time are frozen in the accusative.
When an adverbial takes a following noun, the pair forms an annexation and the following noun is genitive.
The dependent of an adverbial can itself head a further annexation, extending the chain.
The two deictic place words take no dependent and are used to open existential statements.
The lesson's own passages contain adverbial items whose shape is fixed and which therefore fall outside the class-wide accusative rule as stated.

common_mistakes.pattern: marking the noun that follows an adverbial as accusative because the adverbial itself is accusative

proposed_new_units.summary: Per-item table for adverbials of time and place recording, for each member of the closed inventory, whether it is declined or built, whether it obligatorily heads an annexation, what happens when its dependent is omitted, and whether it may itself be governed by a preposition — the facts that decide when an accusative exponent is actually expected and when the case is positional only.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-n04 discriminates the accusative roles from one another but starts from the assumption that a nasb marking has already been read; it holds no lexeme inventory. u-n01 records that built words carry positional case as a general exception but does not say which adverbials are built. Neither prevents the lesson's blanket accusative rule from being projected onto items that never show the exponent.
